arxiv-2101-11966.title: Cubic-scaling all-electron G ​ W GW calculations with a separable density-fitting space-time approach
arxiv-2101-11966.creator: Ivan Duchemin, Xavier Blase
arxiv-2101-11966.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ivan Duchemin, Xavier Blase. We present an implementation of the G ​ W GW space-time approach that allows cubic-scaling all-electron calculations with standard Gaussian basis sets without exploiting any localization nor sparsity considerations. The independent-electron susceptibility is constructed in a time representation over a non-uniform distribution of real-space locations { 𝐫 k } \{{\bf r}_{k}\} optimized within a separable resolution-of-the-identity framework to reproduce standard Coulomb-fitting calculations with meV accuracy.

arxiv-2203-09438.title: An Explainable Stacked Ensemble Model for Static Route-Free Estimation of Time of Arrival
arxiv-2203-09438.creator: Sören Schleibaum, Jörg P. Müller, Monika Sester
arxiv-2203-09438.description: Abstract Sustainable concepts for on-demand transportation, such as ride-sharing or ride-hailing, require advanced technologies and novel dynamic planning and prediction methods. In this paper, we consider the prediction of taxi trip durations, focusing on the problem of ETA ( ETA ). ETA can be used to compute and compare alternative taxi schedules and to provide information to drivers and passengers.

pmc-10562923.title: Optimal evaluation of crop residues for gasification in Ghana using integrated multi-criterial decision making techniques
pmc-10562923.creator: Isaac Osei, Ahmad Addo, Francis Kemausuor
pmc-10562923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Lack of sustainable feedstock quantity and quality has been reported to be one of the major challenges confronting operations of gasifier plants in Ghana. In this paper, TOPSIS (Technique for order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) COPRAS (Complex Proportional Assessment) and VIKOR (Multi-criteria Optimisation and Compromise Solution) were used to select optimal crop residues for sustainable gasification in Ghana among thirteen residue types. The Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) was used as weighting criteria for the three Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques.

pmc-11283391.description: IntroductionUnderstanding why subjects with overweight and with obesity vary in their response to dietary interventions is of major interest for developing personalized strategies for body mass regulation.ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between changes in the urine metabolome and body mass during a breakfast meal intervention.

pmc-11462231.title: Active friction-regulated inertia impact piezoelectric actuator
pmc-11462231.creator: Zhipeng Jin, Xin Song, BaoShan Guo
pmc-11462231.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In inertia impact piezoelectric actuators, the phenomenon of high-frequency drive-induced back-stepping poses a significant limitation to their overall performance. The ultra-fast response time of the piezoelectric stack enables the resolution of this issue. This paper introduces an inertia impact piezoelectric actuator operating under a novel Dual-Stack Motion Mode (DCMM), diverging from the traditional operation in the Single-Stack Motion Mode (STMM) that involves a solitary piezoelectric stack (PES) for active friction control.

pmc-11740050.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) of the recurrent laryngeal nerve during minimally invasive esophagectomy
pmc-11740050.creator: Wenqi Wu, Zhe Zhang, Zhenan Xu, Lening Zhang, Jingyuan Jiang, Fengwu Lin
pmc-11740050.description: BackgroundMinimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) can lead to a severe complication known as recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis (RLNP). Existing literature supports that recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury is the principal etiology of RLNP, a complication potentially mitigated through intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM). In this study, we examined the comprehensive effectiveness of IONM during esophageal resection by performing a meta-analysis.
